full_judgment:
3. The learned Assistant Judge dismissed the said Title Suit No.194 of 1985 on contest by his judgment and decree dated 19.2.1989 and 23.2.1989 respectively. Against which the plaintiff-petitioners filed Title Appeal No.65 of 1989 before the learned District Judge, Bagerhat which was allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court in Title Suit No.194 of 1985 was set aside. Defendant No.1 respondent being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court in Title Appeal No.65 of 1989 moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.I702 of 1994 and obtained a rule. The learned Single Judge by his judgment dated 233.1999 set aside the judgment and decree dated 9.1.1994 and 15.1.1994 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Bagerhat in Title Appeal No.65 of 1989 and made the rule absolute mainly on the ground that the suit land is totally undemarcated and unspecified in the schedule of the plaint and a court shall not be able to pass an executable decree. It also found that the defendant No.1 respondent is in possession of the suit land and a record of right is also running in his name. 

 4. The learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the single Judge of the High Court Division passed the judgment; on mere technicality without discussing the main issues raised in this case and the specific findings of the learned appellate court below. We have considered the submissions of the learned advocate. We find no illegality in the judgment of the High Court Division since the lower appellate court has passed a decree over unspecified and undemarcated suit land which is not executable.
